markingScheme.criterion: Names which connection finished first and which last in the student's own Speed Lanes race, quoting at least two of their own Record rows (e.g. Fibre #1, Cellular #4).
markingScheme.accept: Any ordering that matches the student's own record, including a race with Wi-Fi far away.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating 'cables are fastest' with no reference to the student's own rows.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why: wired and fibre connections have more bandwidth (more data per second) than Wi-Fi and cellular.
markingScheme.accept: 'Wider road / more data at once', 'light is quick', 'Wi-Fi and phone signal are weaker or slower'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Because it is better' with no idea of data amount or speed.

markingScheme.criterion: Compares the packets used by a hub and a switch from the student's own rows (hub 5 or 30, switch 2 or 12) and explains that a hub repeats to everyone while a switch sends only to the target.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct pair of numbers from the record with the repeat-to-all vs target-only explanation.
markingScheme.insufficient: Says a switch is faster without explaining the difference in who receives the packet.

markingScheme.criterion: Chooses a star network for the school.
Names a switch for the middle (not a hub) and says why: it sends data only to the right computer.
markingScheme.accept: 'It knows each computer's address', 'less wasted traffic'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'A hub' with a reason about wasted traffic reversed.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that in a ring a broken cable stops the whole ring because messages pass neighbour to neighbour.
markingScheme.accept: 'Like a game of telephone', 'nothing can get past the break'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'It stops one computer' (that is the star answer).
